title: Prohibition on sale of coordinated pricing algorithms
requirement: Prohibits selling, licensing, or otherwise providing to Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley.
coverage_text: Anyone who sells, licenses, or provides coordinated pricing algorithms (processes using nonpublic Competitor Data less than 90 days old to recommend rents, fees, occupancy rates or other lease terms in coordination between a Berkeley landlord and competitors) to City of Berkeley landlords.
exemptions: Excludes products that publish aggregated, anonymous rental data without recommending rents or terms; products used to set rent or income limits under affordable housing guidelines of a government; and products or processes for market research for project financing, appraisals, or research, testing, or training for software development (if competitor data is not an input when a recommendation is calculated).
penalty: City Attorney may file a civil action for damages, injunctive relief, restitution/return of illegal profits, and/or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation; court shall award reasonable attorney's fees and costs to the City Attorney if prevailing.
quoted_span:
A. It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley 
landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy 
levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.

title: Prohibition on landlord use of coordinated pricing algorithms
requirement: Prohibits landlords from using a coordinated pricing algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley; each month a violation continues and each unit affected is a separate violation.
key_value: civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation
coverage_text: Landlords setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
exemptions: Excludes products that publish aggregated, anonymous rental data without recommending rents or terms; products used to set rent or income limits under affordable housing guidelines of a government; and products or processes for market research for project financing, appraisals, or research, testing, or training for software development (if competitor data is not an input when a recommendation is calculated).
penalty: City Attorney may sue for damages, injunctive relief, restitution/return of illegal profits, and/or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation; an aggrieved tenant may sue for injunctive relief, money damages, and/or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, with reasonable attorney's fees and costs to a prevailing tenant (lease provisions limiting such fees unenforceable).
quoted_span:
B. It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley. Each separate month that a violation exists or continues, and each 
separate residential dwelling unit for which the landlord used the coordinated pricing 
algorithm, shall constitute a separate and distinct violation.

title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance - criminal history prohibition
requirement: Rental housing providers may not ask about or use criminal history or criminal background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection or decision-making. They may not refuse to rent, terminate a tenancy, demand a higher security deposit or rent, refuse to add an immediate family member, or otherwise treat applicants or tenants differently based on criminal history.
coverage_text: Rental housing providers in Berkeley, with regard to current or prospective tenants.
exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; owner-occupied properties (between 1-3 units) in which an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence; units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back to their home in accordance with BMC 13.76.130 A.9; units occupied by existing tenant(s) seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
penalty: Administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation, civil damages including actual damages or three times the amount of one month's rent, punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.
quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; owner-occupied properties (between 1-3 units) in which an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence; units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back to their home in accordance with BMC 13.76.130 A.9; units occupied by existing tenant(s) seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
penalty: Administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation, civil damages including actual damages or three times the amount of one month's rent, punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.
quoted_span: If a landlord takes any action against an applicant or tenant based on criminal history (such as refusing to offer a lease, refusing to add a family member, etc.), the landlord is required to provide the applicant/tenant with written notice and an opportunity to respond.

title: Annual General Adjustment (AGA) cap of 5% (Measure BB)
requirement: The Annual General Adjustment by which a landlord of a fully-covered unit may raise rent each year is set by formula tied to the Consumer Price Index, and may be no more than 5%. A landlord with banked unused AGAs from previous years may still raise rent by more than 5% to reach the rent ceiling.
key_value: AGA set by CPI-linked formula, maximum 5%
coverage_text: Fully-covered rental units under Berkeley's Rent Ordinance. The page lists fully covered unit types as most units in multifamily properties built before 1980, single-family homes with current tenancies that began prior to 1996, and single-family homes with five or more rooms rented out individually; new construction units (certificate of occupancy issued after 1980), most single-family homes and most condominiums are partially covered.
exemptions: Partially covered units (such as new construction with certificate of occupancy issued after 1980, most single-family homes and most condominiums) are not subject to the rent ceiling. Units where the tenant shares kitchen or bath facilities with the landlord are exempt only if the landlord lived in a unit on the same property at the start of the tenancy. The cap does not prevent use of banked AGAs to raise rent to the rent ceiling.
quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.

title: Minimum rental debt for nonpayment eviction
requirement: A landlord may evict for nonpayment of rent only if the tenant owes rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the HUD Fair Market Rent for a unit of equivalent size in the Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR area for the fiscal year in which the rent is demanded.

quoted_span: In any notice terminating a tenancy for a lease breach, the landlord must clearly describe the alleged breach. The landlord must demonstrate that the tenant’s behavior was unreasonable, and may not evict tenants for lease breaches that do not cause the landlord any actual harm.

title: Housing Stability Notification Act - Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources
requirement: Any landlord planning to end a tenancy agreement must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources. It should be delivered at the same time as the Notice to Quit or Notice of Non-renewal of Lease.

title: Housing Stability Notification Act (HSNA)
requirement: A landlord or foreclosing owner ending a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to Quit or notice of non-renewal. The landlord must also send a copy of the Notice to Quit or Notice of Non-renewal, with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, to the City of Boston’s Office of Housing Stability.
coverage_text: All landlords and foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston, including buyers of property out of foreclosure or from a bank or mortgage lender.
exemptions: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; and residences in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse. The requirements may not be waived by lease or agreement.
penalty: Enforced by the Inspectional Services Department: 1st Offense: Warning; 2nd and Subsequent Offenses: $300 per day. A violation does not halt the eviction process.
quoted_span: The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement. The Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources must be delivered at the same time as the Notice to Quit.

title: Source of income discrimination prohibition (FEHA)

penalty: Remedies include recovery of out-of-pocket losses, an injunction, access to the denied housing, damages for emotional distress, civil penalties or punitive damages, and attorney's fees.
quoted_span: California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”). requirement: Housing providers may not consider arrests that did not lead to a conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile justice records, and may not impose blanket bans on all people with a criminal history. exemptions: Drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and lifetime sex offender registration requirements.
penalty: Monetary penalty of not more than $1,000, $5,000 or $10,000 depending on prior violations.
quoted_span: A housing provider shall not knowingly or purposefully publish, or cause to be published, any housing advertisement that explicitly provides that the housing provider will not consider any applicant who has been arrested or convicted of one or more crimes or offenses, except for drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether the applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State sex offender registration program.
effective_date_phrase: This act shall take effect on the first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment

title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - no drug or alcohol testing
requirement: A housing provider may not require an applicant to submit to a drug or alcohol test, or request consent to obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.
coverage_text: Housing providers offering rental dwelling units, other than a dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
penalty: Monetary penalty of not more than $1,000, $5,000 or $10,000 depending on prior violations.
quoted_span: A housing provider shall not require an applicant to submit to a drug or alcohol test, or request the applicant’s consent to obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.
effective_date_phrase: This act shall take effect on the first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment

title: Residential rental property application fee not to exceed $50
requirement: A landlord or its agent may not require an application or similar fee to lease or sublease a residential rental property that exceeds $50. The fee limit is adjusted each year by the Director of the Division of Consumer Affairs in proportion to the percent change in the Consumer Price Index, and only if that change is greater than zero.
key_value: $50 per application, adjusted annually in direct proportion to the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over a 12-month period ending October 31 of the previous year
coverage_text: Landlords and their agents requiring an application or similar fee to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes.
exemptions: Does not apply to a dwelling unit in a one-family or two-family dwelling offered for rent, or to a licensee of the New Jersey Real Estate Commission unless the licensee is the landlord of the residential rental property.
penalty: Penalty of up to $500 for a first offense, up to $750 for a second offense, and up to $1,000 for each subsequent offense, collected through summary proceedings under the Penalty Enforcement Law of 1999; the amount wrongfully charged is taken from the collected penalty and remitted to the applicant or prospective tenant.
quoted_span: A landlord, or agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which exceeds $50.
effective_date_phrase: This act shall take effect on the first day of the fourth month next following the date of enactment

title: Good cause required to refuse lease renewal (Anti-Eviction Act)
requirement: A landlord of residential rental property may not fail to renew any lease, written or oral, unless the landlord has good cause not to renew. Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, motels or hotels, and transient or seasonal units are excepted.
coverage_text: Landlords of residential rental properties, other than owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, motels or hotels, and transient or seasonal units; applies to written and oral leases.
exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient units, and seasonal units.
quoted_span: No landlord of residential rental properties except t hose in owner occupied two or three family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units may fail to renew any lease, regardless of whether it is written or oral unless they have good cause not to renew the lease.

title: Security Deposit Law maximum deposit and annual increase limit
requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit of more than one and one-half times one month's rent. Any additional yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.
key_value: one and one-half (1.5) times one month's rent; yearly increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit
coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes, where the landlord collects a security deposit.
exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are excepted, but a tenant in such a dwelling may make the Security Deposit Law applicable to their tenancy 30 days after sending a written request to the landlord. Landlords are not required to collect a security deposit.
quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less. Any additional yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.

title: Pet security deposit limit
requirement: A landlord may not charge a pet security deposit if, combined with the regular security deposit, it exceeds one and one-half times one month's rent.
key_value: pet deposit plus regular deposit may not exceed one and one-half (1.5) times one month's rent
coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes, where the landlord collects a security deposit.
exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are excepted, but a tenant in such a dwelling may make the Security Deposit Law applicable to their tenancy 30 days after sending a written request to the landlord.
quoted_span: A landlord may not charge a pet security deposit if it exceeds one and one-half times one month’s rent when combined with the regular security deposit.

title: Return of security deposit after lease termination under the Safe Housing Act
requirement: When a tenant terminates a lease early under the Safe Housing Act due to domestic violence, the landlord must make the security deposit plus interest available within 15 business days after termination and notify the tenant in writing within three business days of when and where to pick it up, with a duplicate notice to the relocation officer or municipal clerk. The deposit must be available for thirty (30) days during normal business hours in the municipality, accompanied by an itemized list of interest and deductions.
key_value: return within 15 business days; written notice within three (3) business days; available for thirty (30) days
coverage_text: Tenants who terminate a lease before its expiration as victims of domestic violence under the New Jersey Safe Housing Act.
exemptions: This law does not apply to transient or seasonal rentals.
quoted_span: Within 15 business days after the lease  is terminated, the landlord shall make available the return of the tenant’s security deposit, plus any interest earned, to the tenant or the tenant’s agent. In addition, within three business days after the lease is terminated, the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of when and where the tenant can pick up the security deposit.

title: Security Deposit Law - maximum deposit
requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit of more than one and one-half times one month's rent, and any additional yearly deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. A pet deposit may not be charged if, combined with the regular deposit, it exceeds one and one-half times one month's rent.
key_value: one and one-half (1.5) times one month's rent; yearly increase not to exceed 10% of the current security deposit
coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings (unless the tenant opts in by written request).
exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings; a tenant in such a dwelling may make the law applicable to their tenancy 30 days after sending a written request to the landlord.
quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less. Any additional yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.

title: Prepaid rent counted as security deposit
requirement: Prepaid funds held to secure future rents, including last month's rent, are part of the security deposit; at the inception of the lease the landlord may not require more than two and one-half times the monthly rent, including the deposit and first month's rent.
key_value: two and one-half (2.5) times the monthly rent at lease inception
coverage_text: Rentals covered by the Security Deposit Law.
exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in.
citation: Brownstone Arms v. Asher, 121 N.J. Super. 401 (1972); Reilly v. Weiss, 406 N.J. Super. 71 (2009)
quoted_span: The landlord may only require one and one -half times the tenant’s monthly rent as security and the first month’s rent at the inception of the lease. That means the landlo rd may not require more than two and one-half times the monthly rent at the inception of the lease, this includes the security deposit and the first month’s rent.

title: Security deposit held in trust in interest-bearing account
requirement: Deposit money must be held in trust and not commingled; a landlord receiving deposits for ten or less units must deposit it in an insured New Jersey bank or savings and loan in an interest-bearing account, while landlords with 10 or more units may alternatively use an insured New Jersey-based money market fund or a variable-rate account.
coverage_text: Rentals covered by the Security Deposit Law, other than seasonal use or rental (term of not more than 125 consecutive days by a person with a permanent residence elsewhere).
exemptions: Security deposits for seasonal use or rental (not more than 125 consecutive days by a person having a permanent place of residence elsewhere); does not include housing for seasonal, temporary or migrant farm workers. Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in.
penalty: Any person who unlawfully uses security deposit monies may be criminally charged as a disorderly person and fined not less than $200 or imprisoned for not more than 30 days, or both (N.J.S.A. 46:8-25).
quoted_span: A landlord or designee who receives security deposit money for ten or less units must deposit that money in an insured bank or savings and loan association located in New Jersey in an interest-bearing account at the current interest rate at the time of deposit.

title: Payment of interest on security deposit
requirement: Interest or earnings on the deposit belong to the tenant and must be paid in cash or credited toward rent on the lease renewal or anniversary, or on January 31 if the tenant has been given written notice.
coverage_text: Rentals covered by the Security Deposit Law.
exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in.
quoted_span: The interest or earnings paid on the security deposit belongs to the tenant and shall be paid to the tenant in cash or credited toward rent due and owing on the ren ewal or anniversary of the tenant’s lease or on January 31,  if the tenant has been given written notice, that the interest payments will be paid on January 31 of each year (N.J.S.A. 46:8-19 (c)).

title: Security deposit notice requirements
requirement: Within 30 days of receiving the deposit and at each annual interest payment, the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the institution's name and address, deposit amount, account type and interest rate; the landlord must also notify the tenant within 30 days of transferring the deposit to a new landlord or account.
key_value: within 30 days
coverage_text: Rentals covered by the Security Deposit Law.
exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in.
penalty: If the tenant does not receive proper notice or interest, the tenant may give written notice that the security money plus interest at 7% per annum be applied to rent; for missed annual notice or interest the landlord has 30 days to comply first, and the landlord may not demand an additional deposit afterward.
quoted_span: Within 30 days of receipt of the security deposit and at t he time of each annual interest payment, the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the name and address of the banking institution or investment company in which the money is deposited, the amount of the deposit, type of account, and current rate o f interest for the account.

title: Return of security deposit after termination
requirement: Within 30 days after termination of a tenancy, the landlord must return the deposit plus interest less deductions by personal delivery, registered or certified mail, with an itemized list of any deductions sent by registered or certified mail. No deductions may be made from the deposit of a tenant who remains in possession.
key_value: within 30 days after termination of tenancy
coverage_text: Rentals covered by the Security Deposit Law.
exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in.
penalty: The court may award the tenant double the amount wrongly withheld, together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
quoted_span: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1).

title: Return of security deposit upon displacement
requirement: Within five (5) business days after a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation (when an official has posted a notice prohibiting occupancy or certified displacement longer than seven (7) days), the landlord must return the deposit, and within three (3) business days of notice must tell the tenant where it can be collected.
key_value: five (5) business days
coverage_text: Tenants displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation in rentals covered by the Security Deposit Law.
exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in.
quoted_span: Within five (5) business days after a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or evacuation, the landlord must return the security deposit.

title: Security deposit on sale or transfer of property
requirement: When the property is sold or transferred, the new owner must obtain the deposit plus accrued interest from the former owner and is responsible for investing it, giving notices, paying interest and returning it.
coverage_text: Rentals covered by the Security Deposit Law that are sold or transferred.
exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in.
quoted_span: If the property is sold or transferred it is the duty of the new owner to obtain the security deposit, plus accrued interest on the tenant’s deposit, that was collected by the former owner.

title: Penalty for withholding deposits of assisted tenants
requirement: A landlord who willfully and intentionally withholds a deposit made by or for a tenant receiving State or federal financial assistance may be liable for a civil penalty of not less than $500 or not more than $2,000 per offense.
key_value: not less than $500 or not more than $2,000 for each offense
coverage_text: Security deposits made by or on behalf of tenants who received financial assistance through any State or federal program, including welfare or rental assistance.
penalty: Civil penalty of not less than $500 or not more than $2,000 for each offense, collected under the Penalty Enforcement Law (N.J.S.A. 2A:58-12).
quoted_span: Any landlord who willfully and intentionally withholds a security deposit made by or on behalf of a tenant who has received financial assistance through any Stat e or federal program, including welfare or rental assistance , may be penalized. The landlord may be liable for a civil penalty of not less than $500 or not more than $2,000 for each offense.

title: New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD) - housing
requirement: Landlords may not refuse to rent or discriminate in rental housing based on protected characteristics, including source of lawful income.
coverage_text: All landlord-tenant relationships, except two-family owner-occupied dwellings, rooms in an owner- or resident-occupied single home, and single-sex residences and age-restricted housing as to familial status.
exemptions: Two-family owner occupied dwellings; rooms in an owner or resident-occupied single home; residences planned exclusively for and occupied by one sex (e.g. YMCA) and age-restricted housing, as it pertains to familial status.
penalty: Monetary damages and possible requirement to rent the unit to the complainant; fines and penalties up to $10,000 for a first offense (N.J.S.A. 10:5-14.1a(a)).
quoted_span: The New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD), N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h), prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender  identity or expression, mental and physical disability, nationality, or source of lawful income.

title: Unconscionable rent increase prohibition (Anti-Eviction Act)
requirement: A rent increase must not be unconscionable, meaning so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest person, and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases. Before evicting a tenant for nonpayment of an increased rent, the owner must first serve a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase.
coverage_text: Residential tenants facing a rent increase; where no municipal rent control exists, a judge decides in an eviction action whether the increase was unconscionable.
quoted_span: The increase in rent must not be unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.
interaction_text: must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases

title: No mid-lease rent increase; lease termination notice for rent increase
requirement: A landlord cannot raise the rent mid-lease term; the old lease must be terminated with proper written notice and the tenant offered a new lease at the increased rent. The written notice must state that the tenant can remain by signing a new lease at the increased rent.
coverage_text: Landlords seeking to increase rent on residential tenants.
quoted_span: A landlord cannot raise the rent mid-lease term. The old lease must be terminated, and the new lease must have the increased rental payment.

title: Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law exemption from local rent control
requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from any local rent control ordinances for 30 years following completion of construction of the building.
key_value: 30 years following completion of construction
coverage_text: Newly constructed multiple dwellings within 30 years after completion of construction.
quoted_span: Under the Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law ( N.J.S.A. 2A:42 -84.5), newly constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.
interaction_text: newly constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction of the building

title: No rent increase for condominium/cooperative conversion costs
requirement: If a building is converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion. Rents may still be increased to cover the cost of new services or amenities.
coverage_text: All tenants in a building converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership, regardless of eligibility for protected tenancy as senior citizens or disabled persons.
exemptions: Increases to cover the cost of new services or amenities are not barred.
quoted_span: If a building is converted to a condominium or cooperative form of ownership, or to fee simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the conversion (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.31).

title: Credit report cost and rental application fees
requirement: A landlord may charge a prospective tenant for the cost of a credit report and may request reasonable rental application fees or employment verification.
coverage_text: Landlords screening prospective tenants.
quoted_span: The landlord is allowed to charge the tenant for the cost of the report. The landlord may also request reasonable rental application fees or employment verification.

title: Anti-Eviction Act: good cause required to evict or not renew
requirement: A residential landlord may not evict a tenant or fail to renew a written or oral lease without good cause, and must be able to prove the grounds for eviction in court.
coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including single-family homes, mobile homes and land in a mobile home park, apartment buildings, complexes, and rooming and boarding homes.
exemptions: May not apply to two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units. Does not apply to hotel guests, motel guests, or guest houses rented to a transient guest or seasonal tenant, except hotel and motel guests with no alternate residence who reside there on a continual basis. Does not apply to a unit held in trust on behalf of a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies the unit.
quoted_span: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause.

title: Anti-Eviction Act: written Notice to Quit
requirement: Each good cause, except nonpayment of rent, must be described in detail in a written notice to the tenant, and a Notice to Quit is required for all good cause evictions except for nonpayment of rent.
coverage_text: Residential rental properties covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
exemptions: Not required for an eviction for nonpayment of rent.
quoted_span: Each cause, except for nonpayment of rent, must be described in detail by the landlord in a written notice to the tenant. A “Notice to Quit” is required for all good cause evictions, except for an eviction for nonpayment of rent ( N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2).

title: Eviction ground: failure to pay rent
requirement: A landlord may bring an eviction action for nonpayment of rent without prior notice, except that a 14-day notice is required if the tenant resides in federally subsidized housing. A tenant may not be evicted for nonpayment if the unpaid rent was used to continue landlord-responsible utility services (electric, gas, water, sewer) after notice of discontinuance.
key_value: 14-day notice for federally subsidized housing
coverage_text: Tenants in residential rental properties covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
exemptions: No eviction for nonpayment where the tenant used the unpaid rent to continue utility services the landlord was responsible for and failed to pay.
quoted_span: If a tenant fails to pay rent, the landlord may immediately take legal action to have the tenant evicted. The landlord is not required to give the tenant notice before filing an eviction suit, except if the tenant resides in federally subsidized housing.

title: Eviction ground: disorderly conduct
requirement: If, after a written Notice to Cease, the tenant continues disorderly conduct that destroys the peace and quiet of other tenants or the neighborhood, the landlord may sue for eviction after serving a Notice to Quit at least three days before filing.
key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days prior to filing
coverage_text: Tenants in residential rental properties covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(b)).

title: Eviction ground: damage or destruction to the property
requirement: A tenant may be evicted for intentionally or by gross negligence causing or allowing destruction, damage, or injury to the property; a Notice to Quit must be served at least three days before filing suit.
key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days prior to filing
coverage_text: Tenants in residential rental properties covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
quoted_span: The tenant may be evicted if they have intentionally or by reason of gross negligence caused or allowed destruction, damage, or injury to the property.

title: Eviction ground: substantial violation of landlord's rules and regulations
requirement: If, after a written Notice to Cease, the tenant continues to substantially violate reasonable rules in the lease or accepted in writing, the landlord may sue for eviction after serving a Notice to Quit at least one month before filing, with notices given on or before the start of a new month.
key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month prior to filing
coverage_text: Tenants in residential rental properties covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month prior to filing the suit for eviction.

title: Nonpayment of rent: utility payment defense
requirement: A tenant may not be evicted for nonpayment of rent if the tenant used the unpaid rent to keep utility services (electric, gas, water, sewer) going after notice of discontinuance, where the landlord was responsible for those utilities and did not pay. Money so used counts as part of the rent payment.
coverage_text: Tenants facing eviction for nonpayment of rent where the landlord was responsible for utility payments.
quoted_span: Note: A tenant may not be evicted for nonpayment of rent, if the tenant used the unpaid portion of rent to continue utility services to the rental premises after receiving notice that the services were in danger of being discontinued, and if the landlord was responsible for the payment of those utility services and did not make the payments required to retain the us e of those services.

title: Eviction cause: disorderly conduct
requirement: The landlord may file for eviction if, after a written Notice to Cease, the tenant continues disorderly conduct that destroys the peace and quiet of other tenants or the neighborhood. A Notice to Quit must be served at least three days before filing.
key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days prior to filing
quoted_span: If after given written Notice to Cease disorderly conduct, the tenant continues the disorderly conduct and that conduct destroys the peace and quiet of the other tenants living in the building or neighborhood, the landlord may file a suite for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(b)).

title: Eviction cause: damage or destruction to the property
requirement: A tenant may be evicted for intentionally or through gross negligence causing or allowing destruction, damage or injury to the property. A Notice to Quit must be served at least three days before filing.
key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days prior to filing
quoted_span: The tenant may be evicted if they have intentionally or by reason of gross negligence caused or allowed destruction, damage, or injury to the property.

title: Eviction cause: substantial violation of landlord's rules and regulations
requirement: After a written Notice to Cease, a tenant who continues to substantially violate reasonable rules in the lease or accepted in writing may be sued for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served at least one month before filing, and notices must be given on or before the start of a new month.
key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month prior to filing
quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month prior to filing the suit for eviction. In addition, any notices must be given on or before the start of a new month (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(d)).

title: Eviction cause: breach of lease covenants
requirement: If the tenant continues to substantially breach reasonable lease covenants after a written Notice to Cease and the lease reserves a right of re-entry, the landlord may file for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served at least one month before filing.
key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month prior to filing
coverage_text: Leases in which the landlord has reserved a right of re-entry.
quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month prior to filing the suit for this type of eviction.

title: Eviction cause: public housing lease breach involving drugs or illegal activity
requirement: In public housing, the landlord may file for eviction if the tenant substantially breached lease covenants about illegal drug use or other illegal activities; the covenant must conform to federal guidelines and be in effect at the start of the lease. No Notice to Cease is required; the Notice to Quit follows federal public housing regulations.
coverage_text: Public housing.
quoted_span: 2) In public housing, if the tenant has substantially violated or breached any of the covenants or agreements contained in the lease, pertaining to illegal uses of controlled dangerous substances, or other illegal activities, the landlord may file a suit for eviction.

title: Eviction cause: failure to pay rent increase
requirement: If a tenant fails to pay rent after notice of a rent increase and a Notice to Quit, the landlord may file for eviction; the increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with other laws including rent control. A Notice to Quit must be served at least one month before filing.
key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month prior to filing
quoted_span: If a tenant fails to pay rent after being given notice of a rent increase and a Notice to Quit, the landlord may file a suit for eviction.
interaction_text: must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control

title: Rent increase must not be unconscionable
requirement: A rent increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control. A tenant who believes an increase is unconscionable may withhold the difference between the old and new rent, and the court decides.
quoted_span: The rent increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control.
interaction_text: must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control

title: Eviction cause: health and safety violations or removal from rental market
requirement: A tenant may be evicted where the landlord must board up or demolish for substantial violations, cannot abate violations with the tenant present, must correct an illegal occupancy, or a government agency removes the property from the rental market. A Notice to Quit must be served at least three months before filing, and the tenant cannot be evicted until relocation assistance is provided.
key_value: Notice to Quit at least three months before filing
quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three months before filing a suit for eviction. The tenant can’t be evicted until relocation assistance is provided.

title: Relocation assistance for illegal occupancy evictions
requirement: A tenant evicted for illegal occupancy is entitled to relocation assistance equal to six times the monthly rent, paid by the landlord at least five days before removal. If unpaid and no municipal fund exists, interest accrues at 18% per year and the amount due is a lien on the property.
key_value: six times the tenant’s monthly rent
coverage_text: Tenants evicted under cause G 3) (illegal occupancy).
penalty: Interest accrues on the unpaid balance at the rate of 18% per year; the amount due is a lien on the property; landlord must repay the municipality's relocation fund.
quoted_span: Any tenant evicted under G 3) (illegal occupancy) is entitled to relocation assistance in an amount equal to six times the tenant’s monthly rent.

title: Eviction cause: permanent retirement from residential use
requirement: A landlord who wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential use may file for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served at least 18 months before filing, and no action may be taken until the lease expires.
key_value: Notice to Quit at least 18 months prior to filing
coverage_text: Buildings or mobile home parks being permanently retired from residential use.
exemptions: Does not apply where the circumstances in section (G) apply.
quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least 18 months prior to filing the suit for eviction.

title: Eviction cause: refusal to accept reasonable lease changes
requirement: At lease expiration, if the tenant refuses reasonable but substantial changes after written notice, the landlord may file for eviction and the court decides reasonableness. A Notice to Quit must be served at least one month before filing.
key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month before filing
quoted_span: If after written notice the tenant refuses to accept those changes the landlord may file a suit for eviction and the court will determine if the proposed changes are reasonable.

title: Eviction cause: continual nonpayment or habitual late payment
requirement: If the tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late after a written Notice to Cease, the landlord may file for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served at least one month before filing.
key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month before filing
quoted_span: If the tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late, after written Notice to Cease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month before filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(j)).

title: Eviction cause: conversion to condominium, cooperative or fee simple
requirement: A landlord converting a building or mobile home park to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership may file for eviction after complying with conversion regulations; a Notice to Quit must be served at least three years before filing and no action until the lease expires. Courts may grant up to five one-year stays, and no action may be brought against protected senior citizen or disabled tenants.
key_value: Notice to Quit at least three years before filing
coverage_text: Buildings or mobile home parks being converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership of two or more units or sites.
exemptions: No action against a senior citizen or disabled tenant with protected tenancy status under the Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act.
quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be ser ved on the tenant at least three years before filing a suit for eviction.

title: Eviction cause: post-conversion tenancy, sale to owner-occupant

title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing: sale and licensing of algorithmic devices
requirement: Proposed ordinance would make it unlawful for any person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord.
